events.title: The sacred chickens
events.text: The consul Publius Claudius Pulcher ignores the omens, by tradition throwing the sacred chickens overboard, and sails for Drepana.

events.title: Battle of Drepana
events.text: The Carthaginian admiral Adherbal pins the Roman fleet against the shore and takes ninety-three of its 123 ships.

events.title: Carthalo strikes
events.text: The Carthaginian Carthalo attacks the Roman ships off Lilybaeum, burning some and towing others away.

events.title: Wrecked off Camarina
events.text: A storm destroys the fleet of the consul Lucius Junius Pullus and its supply convoy on the south coast.

events.title: Rome seizes Eryx
events.text: Junius Pullus takes the mountain town of Eryx and its famous temple, above Drepana.

events.title: A dictator in Sicily
events.text: Aulus Atilius Calatinus becomes the first dictator to lead an army outside Italy.

events.title: Hiero's alliance
events.text: Rome makes its treaty with Hiero II of Syracuse permanent; his grain feeds the besiegers.

events.title: Siege of Lilybaeum
events.text: Without a fleet, the Romans hold their siege lines around Lilybaeum by land alone.

events.title: Carthage's raids
events.text: Carthaginian squadrons raid the coasts of Italy and Roman Sicily almost unopposed.

events.title: Hamilcar Barca arrives
events.text: Hamilcar Barca takes command in Sicily and seizes Mount Heircte above Panormus.

events.title: Raid on Bruttium
events.text: Hamilcar's ships plunder the coast of Locri and Bruttium.

events.title: Raid toward Cumae
events.text: Carthaginian raiders range up the Italian coast as far as Cumae.

events.title: Hanno in Africa
events.text: Hanno the Great campaigns in the Libyan interior and takes Theveste.

events.title: Hannibal is born
events.text: Hamilcar's son Hannibal is born at about this time in Carthage.

events.title: Claudia's fine
events.text: Pulcher's sister is fined for wishing aloud that her brother could lose another fleet and thin the crowds.

events.title: Privateers at Hippo
events.text: Privately fitted Roman ships raid the African port of Hippo, near Utica.

events.title: War on the mountain
events.text: Hamilcar's men and the Roman army skirmish for years around Panormus.

events.title: Stalemate
events.text: Neither side can drive the other out of western Sicily.

events.title: Raiders on the coast
events.text: Hamilcar's ships keep raiding the Italian coast, while Roman privateers prey on Africa.

events.title: Hamilcar takes Eryx
events.text: Hamilcar moves by sea and seizes the town of Eryx, between the Roman posts above and below.

events.title: Colony at Brundisium
events.text: Rome plants a Latin colony at Brundisium, its future gateway to the East.

events.title: Siege within a siege
events.text: At Eryx, Hamilcar is besieged on the mountain while besieging the Romans on its summit.

events.title: An empty treasury
events.text: After twenty years of war and four lost fleets, Rome's treasury cannot pay for another.

events.title: Carthage saves money
events.text: Believing Rome beaten at sea, Carthage lays up most of its warships.

events.title: A fleet on credit
events.text: Wealthy Romans, alone or in groups of two or three, each pay for a fully equipped warship.

events.title: The Rhodian's ship
events.text: The new ships copy a fast Carthaginian blockade runner captured off Lilybaeum.

events.title: Catulus sails
events.text: The consul Gaius Lutatius Catulus arrives off Drepana with two hundred quinqueremes.

events.title: Catulus wounded
events.text: Catulus is wounded in the thigh during an assault on Drepana.

events.title: Blockade of Lilybaeum
events.text: The Roman fleet closes the harbours of Lilybaeum and Drepana.

events.title: Drills at sea
events.text: Through the winter Catulus trains his crews daily, rowing and manoeuvring.

events.title: Hanno's convoy
events.text: Carthage sends a hastily manned relief fleet, low in the water with grain for Hamilcar.

events.title: Landfall at Hiera
events.text: Hanno's fleet gathers at the island of Hiera, now Marettimo, to wait for a fair wind.

events.title: Catulus at Aegusa
events.text: Catulus crosses to Aegusa, now Favignana, to bar the way to Eryx.

events.title: Battle of the Aegates
events.text: On 10 March, Catulus attacks into the wind; Carthage loses fifty ships sunk and seventy captured.

events.title: Hanno crucified
events.text: Hanno, the defeated admiral, is executed in Carthage.

events.title: Hamilcar negotiates
events.text: Given full powers, Hamilcar sends Gisco to treat with Catulus.

events.title: Treaty of Lutatius
events.text: Rome's assembly toughens the terms: Carthage leaves Sicily and pays 3,200 talents in ten years.

events.title: Sicily evacuated
events.text: Gisco ships the garrison of Lilybaeum home to Africa in groups.

events.title: Lipari ceded
events.text: Carthage gives up the islands between Sicily and Italy.

events.title: Malta stays Punic
events.text: Malta remains Carthaginian for another twenty-three years.

events.title: Mercenaries unpaid
events.text: The returning mercenaries gather at Sicca, unpaid; their revolt will become a war.

events.title: Syracuse endures
events.text: Hiero II keeps his kingdom, the only independent state left in Sicily.

chartNote: Share of the mapped area (today's provinces of southern Italy, Sicily and Sardinia, plus Tunisia and Malta) by who controlled it. A simplification: control was held town by town, regions are modern boundaries, and Tunisia stands for Carthage's African lands, whose inland reach is uncertain. The war at sea, which decided everything, does not show on a land map.
